newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Bank Austria to offer early CA share swap.
newsitem.headline: Bank Austria to offer early CA share swap.

text.p: Bank Austria said on Monday it would make an offer to Creditanstalt shareholders to swap their shares and participation certificates for Bank Austria stock as soon as possible.
Bank Austria, the nation's biggest bank, gained European Commission approval for the takeover of its nearest rival Creditanstalt last week.

Under the terms of the deal, struck with the Austrian government in January, Bank Austria agreed to buy out shareholders by offering them its shares. Small shareholders would also be given the option of 722.5 schillings cash.

"We will start immediately with an evaluation to enable us to decide on the exchange ratio. We will press for the exchange to go ahead as quickly as possible, though realistically it will probably take a few months," Bank Austria chief executive Gerhard Randa told a news conference.

He forecast the exchange would go ahead in the late summer or early autumn, once auditors Deloitte & Touche, KPMG and investment banks Salomon Brothers and J.P. Morgan had assessed the value of Bank Austria and Creditanstalt shares based on the banks' 1996 performances.

"On the basis of their valuation we will come up with a fair ratio and propose to Creditanstalt shareholders that they exchange their shares or participation certificates for Bank Austria shares or participation certificates," Randa said.
"I expect the offer will be well received.
Under the taekover agreement, the City of Vienna also agreed to reduce its influence on Bank Austria through its holding company AVZ.

Randa said if all Creditanstalt shareholders took advantage of the swap offer, AVZ's Bank Austria holding would fall to below 30 percent from 40 percent at present. Its ordinary shareholding would decline to 30 percent from 45 percent.
"In that instance the target of reducing the stake to below 25 percent over five years would be as good as reached," Randa said. -- Janet McBride, Vienna newsroom +43-1 531 12 254
